newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Patria revises '96 GDP estimate downward.
newsitem.headline: Czech Patria revises '96 GDP estimate downward.

text.p: Investment bank Patria Finance on Monday said it had revised downward its 1996 full year GDP forecast for the Czech Republic to 4.5 percent from a previous estimate of 5.5 percent.
"The preliminary GDP growth (of 4.0 percent) as reported for the second quarter by the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) last week was significantly lower than we expected," Patria said in a statement.
"On this basis, Patria has revised its full year forecast from 5.5 percent to 4.5 percent. For the year 1997, we see real GDP growth of 4.5-5 percent," the statement added.
The CSU released figures last week showing real Czech economic growth for the second quarter slowed to 4.0 percent year-on-year, after 4.6 percent growth in the first quarter.
Analysts said they were disappointed with the figures which compare unfavourably with neighbouring countries such as Slovakia which posted second quarter growth of just under seven percent.

They added that responsibility for the downturn could partly be attributed to the sluggish performance of many of the Czech Republic's major trading partners in the European Union and some said the government should do more to boost exports.

"In the third quarter, we expect growth to accelerate. A large part of this will be attributable to the fact that there are two more working days than in the same quarter in the previous year," Patria said.
"It will also be supported by an upturn in growth in western Europe," the statement said.
